title: Snowflake ID generator
summary: Pack a millisecond timestamp, a worker ID and a per-millisecond sequence into 64-bit IDs that are unique and time-ordered, surviving sequence overflow and a clock that goes backwards.

complexity.time: O(1), except waiting out the rest of a millisecond after 4,096 IDs

hints: The ID is three integers glued together with shifts: (ms since epoch) << 22, worker << 12, sequence in the low 12 bits. Uniqueness comes from never reusing the same (timestamp, worker, sequence) triple.
Keep two pieces of state: the last timestamp you issued and the sequence used in it. Compare each fresh clock reading against the last timestamp: behind, equal, or ahead are three different cases.

Behind: raise. Equal: sequence = (sequence + 1) & 4095, and if that wrapped to 0, keep calling now() until it returns a later millisecond. Ahead: sequence = 0. Then store the timestamp and assemble. parse reverses it with >> and & masks.
